title: When the Choir Turns
premise: Hazel Eriksen, a hedge-charmer hiding his forbidden gift in the occupied free city of Vellsmark, discovers the old gods are answering prayers again—and that he is the last living vessel of the Choir, an inherited bloodline that once bound gods to mortal will. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and courted by a resistance that wants to weaponize him, Hazel must choose between revealing his identity to save the free cities or staying silent as the ancient war reignites. In the end, Hazel refuses both sides: he unbinds the gods entirely, sacrificing his own magic and the guild's legacy, so that neither empire nor rebellion can claim divine power—buying the free cities freedom at the cost of everything he was.
about_author: Ada Okonkwo is a former church archivist from Lagos who writes fantasy about faith, inheritance, and the people history forgets. Her short fiction has appeared in several anthologies; When the Choir Turns is her debut novel.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He sells luck-knots and fever-salves in Vellsmark's night market, carefully mundane enough to evade the magical proscription. A desperate mother's prayer seems to actually work through one of his charms. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the first crack in three years of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: The Guild of Nine Names
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He visits Magda, the last senior member of his dying guild, who confirms rumors: prayers are being answered across the city, and only bloodline vessels can hear it. She warns him never to pray aloud. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited obligation pressing on a man who wanted nothing.

chapters.title: What the Mother Knew
chapters.summary: The mother, Ilse, POV. Her son's fever broke impossibly fast, and she tells an inquisitor's clerk about the charming young man from the market. Emotional beat: gratitude curdling into guilt as she realizes what she has set in motion.

chapters.title: Grey Coats in the Market
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Inquisitors sweep the night market; Hazel escapes by using a small working in public for the first time, witnessed by a stranger named Corvin. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration—the invisibility is already gone.

chapters.title: Corvin's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. The stranger reveals himself as a resistance courier and offers Hazel sanctuary with the Lantern Cell, claiming they can protect vessels like him. Emotional beat: seductive hope shadowed by the sense of being recruited rather than rescued.

chapters.title: Magda's Confession
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Dying Magda admits the guild didn't just serve the old gods—they imprisoned them, binding them into the Choir so mortals could control divine power. Hazel is the final knot in that binding. Emotional beat: betrayal; his whole identity reframed as a cage.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs across Vellsmark. Miracles spread—a drowned child breathes, a blighted field greens—and the usurper's armies turn toward the free cities, drawn by the resurgence. Emotional beat: wonder tipping into collective fear.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Question
chapters.summary: Inquisitor-General Vane's POV. He interrogates captured guild records and learns a vessel lives in Vellsmark; he orders the city sealed. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace—he doesn't want to kill the vessel, he wants to use him.

chapters.title: Into the Lantern Cell
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He shelters with the resistance, meeting their leader, Sera, who believes the gods' return means liberation. They ask him to sing the Choir's opening verse to rally the faithful. Emotional beat: belonging offered at the price of becoming a symbol.

chapters.title: The First Verse
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Alone, he tries the verse and hears the bound gods answer—not grateful, but furious, straining against three centuries of imprisonment. One of them speaks his name. Emotional beat: awe laced with horror; the inheritance is a hostage situation.

chapters.title: Sera's Truth
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She knows what the Choir did and intends to keep the gods bound but aimed at the usurper—a weapon, not a liberation. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth; she loves the cause more than honesty.

chapters.title: The Sealed City
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Vane's troops close the gates; food runs short; the resistance plans to trigger the Choir publicly to spark uprising before the army arrives. Emotional beat: claustrophobic urgency, ordinary suffering around extraordinary stakes.

chapters.title: Ilse Returns
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She finds Hazel and begs forgiveness, then offers the one thing she has: knowledge of the inquisitors' movements, gained cleaning their barracks. Emotional beat: redemption through small, dangerous acts.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Captured briefly by Vane, Hazel is offered a deal: surrender willingly, and the city opens. Vane reveals the usurper also descends from guild blood—an heir who wants the Choir for the empire. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Broken Knot
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Escaping with Corvin's help, Hazel decides the binding itself must end—but unbinding may release gods with three centuries of rage. Emotional beat: resolve born of refusal; he will not be anyone's weapon.

chapters.title: Sera's Gamble
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Learning Hazel's intent, she moves the uprising forward without him, planning to force the Choir open during the festival crowd. Emotional beat: tragic conviction—she'd burn the truth to save the cause.

chapters.title: Festival of Ashes
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel, Sera, and Vane POVs. At the harvest festival, resistance and inquisition collide; Sera begins the rite with stolen guild words, and the sky splits. Emotional beat: chaos, courage, and catastrophe interwoven.

chapters.title: The Gods Unbound
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He reaches the rite's heart and sings the unbinding instead, taking the full weight of the Choir into himself. The gods pour free—vast, wounded, and listening. Emotional beat: transcendence and self-erasure; he gives up his magic and perhaps his life.

chapters.title: What the Gods Chose
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The freed gods withdraw beyond mortal reach, sparing the city but stripping all vessels—including the usurper's bloodline—of power. His armies stall; the war gutters out. Emotional beat: stunned silence where victory should roar.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Vellsmark
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The city mourns and rebuilds; Sera, broken by what she nearly caused, disbands the Lantern Cell. Hazel survives, hollowed, unrecognized in the market he once worked. Emotional beat: grief braided with fragile peace.

chapters.title: A Man Without Magic
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. He tends Ilse's recovered son with ordinary medicine and finds that a life unbound from legacy might be his first truly chosen one. Corvin asks what he'll do now. Emotional beat: quiet hope; identity rebuilt from choice, not inheritance.

chapters.title: When the Choir Turns
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. On a hill above Vellsmark, Hazel feels something faint answer a stranger's prayer—not the old gods, not the Choir, something new and gentle. He smiles, keeps walking, and tells no one. Emotional beat: closure with an open door; the world, like Hazel, is free to become.
